title: Cross-route burst siphon due to stale policy priority index
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed a scenario where transient route-level bursts were being drained against unrelated org keys when a policy refresh coincided with an in-flight request window. Root cause hypothesis: stale 'priority index' state in the policy cache allowed older priority assignments to be used for enforcement decisions, causing credits to be debited from a parent org allowance instead of the route-scoped bucket. This manifests as quiet overdraws on org quotas and surprising throttles for routes that should have been shielded.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a route config with recent policy change (increase route weight) and immediately send a short burst of requests aligned to the policy refresh window
Force a policy cache refresh on a subset of edge shards (simulate rollout across shards)
Observe billing/credit attribution in Grafana: org-level allowance decreases even though requests were tagged with route-scoped keys
observed_metrics: Grafana dashboard: rate-engine->credits->per-org shows ~12% unexpected dip during refresh window
Trace sample: trace ID trc_20260302_0912 shows enforcement decision used priority_index v12 (stale) while policy version header indicates v15
Metering exporter logs: 5 instances of 'applied-bucket=org-default' when route-bucket should have been chosen
current_findings: Policy cache TTL is short (30s) but our refresh path applies delta merges that leave a priority_index field untouched when route-level overrides are present
Enforcement path reads priority_index from an auxiliary in-memory map which is updated asynchronously; races can yield a miss and fallback to parent index
Shard-local rollout ordering means different edge nodes can evaluate with different snapshot orders leading to cross-shard siphoning
proposed_fix: Ensure full atomic swap of policy snapshot on refresh instead of piecemeal delta merge; include priority_index in the atomic payload
Update enforcement logic to prefer explicit route-bucket match when request metadata contains route_id and route_bucket exists
Add short-lived instrumentation to detect enforcement decisions that choose parent buckets during a refresh window and emit an alert
work_done: Added reproducer script and test harness that simulates staggered shard refreshes (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/2683)
Captured flamegraphs and perf traces for enforcement hot path showing the async read of priority_index (link: https://grafana.redwood/s/trace/2683)
Created temporary Canaries to route 10% of traffic to a branch with atomic snapshot swap to validate fix impact
blocking_issues: Needs review from policy-team for snapshot contract change (ENG-600999)
Integration tests flake under CI due to timing (ENG-601000)
acceptance_criteria: No unexpected org-level credit drains observed during forced policy refresh in the reproducer
End-to-end tests added to CI that simulate concurrent refresh+burst and consistently pass
Rollback-safe rollout plan documented and validated on staging with canary traffic
notes: Mitigation: temporarily disable concurrent partial merges by enabling 'serialize-policy-refresh' flag on edge nodes until fix ships
Customer impact: several large customers reported unexplained quota reductions during a previous rollout; correlate their timestamps with policy refresh logs
Follow-up: evaluate making policy snapshots backward-compatible to avoid similar races when we add new enforcement fields
